title: Loopback — rotation circuit puzzle
summary: Build Loopback, a complete single-file browser puzzle game: rotate wire tiles to power every lamp across twelve verified-solvable levels, with sequential unlocking, best-score persistence, full keyboard play, and an editorial-lab visual identity. Deterministic rules make runs comparable.

provenance.attribution: Challenge authored for the OneShot library.
provenance.notes: Draft challenge authored for OneShot. Its circuit-rotation loop is genre-established and its title has a public collision; it remains closed pending naming and final originality review. The disputed result remains tied to archived v1.0.0; v1.0.1 only clarifies the execution-workflow heading and labels the example level rows for audit cleanliness. It is not an activation.

capabilities.environment: Autonomous coding agent with file and shell access; artifact must run offline from file:// in current Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari.
constraints: Single self-contained index.html; no build step, framework, or external asset required to play.

budget.notes: Generous single-run budget; internal testing and level-solvability scripting are expected within the one brief.

verification.description: index.html opens via file:// with zero console errors and no external URLs in source.
Rotating tiles changes connectivity; lamps light exactly when connected; completion requires all lamps lit.
All twelve levels were solved at or below par by the executor, with per-level move counts recorded.
Best scores survive reload; corrupted localStorage falls back to a fresh profile without errors.
Levels 1 through 3 are completable using only the keyboard.

artifacts.description: Run instructions, rules summary, assumptions, and honest verification record.

one_shot_policy.notes: One initial brief; executors are expected to test, verify solvability, and repair defects within the same run.

benchmark_question: Can an agent deliver a deterministic, keyboard-complete puzzle loop with reliable progression and recovery in one offline HTML file?
